newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian premier opens dialogue with rebels.
newsitem.headline: Albanian premier opens dialogue with rebels.

text.p: Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino has opened a dialogue with rebels who control most of the south in a bid to end weeks of turmoil in Europe's poorest country.

Fino, a member of the opposition Socialists heading an all-party national unity government, met leaders from the rebel stronghold of Vlore on Friday for the first time since taking office earlier this month.
The new premier, who is himself from the south and a former mayor of rebel-held Gjirokaster, appealed for all sides to work together to prevent the disintegration of the country.
Earlier the premier rebuffed the rebels by dismissing their calls for the resignation of President Sali Berisha, blamed for not stopping dubious savings schemes that bankrupted thousands.

In an interview with Reuters, Fino said Berisha's resignation would cause a power vacuum in a country still reeling from weeks of looting and shooting by Albanians angry at the loss of their money in the failed schemes.
Berisha himself, in a rare public statement, called on Albanians to work together to resolve the current crisis.

"All Albanians should overcome the situation and look towards the future...We have not lost our trust in the future, our trust in democracy or in the European orientation of the country, which remain fundamental principles," he said at a Moslem ceremony in Tirana.
Fino has been locked in a power struggle with Berisha's Democratic Party, which holds 122 of the 140 seats in parliament after elections last May that international observers said were deeply flawed.
"The government has a more important mission than asking for the president's resignation," Fino said. "It would create an institutional vacuum if Berisha were to resign."
Leaders of most political parties represented in the government have made clear they want an end to Berisha's presidency, but would prefer this was brought about by democratic means.
Berisha has promised to quit if his party loses new elections to be held by June.

Fino was speaking a day after rebel leaders from 14 towns in southern Albania issued a fresh call for Berisha to resign, but pulled back from a confrontation with the government by dropping plans to set up a rival leadership in the south.
Participants at the meeting promised Fino they would stabilise the situation in Vlore so it could serve as an example for the whole country, television reported.

Vlore, along with other rebel-held towns in the south, is ostensibly under the control of citizens' councils but wracked by widespread lawlessness following the looting of weapons from army depots at the start of the revolt.

Italy was preparing to send emergency health supplies to Albania following a request from Fino. The Foreign Ministry in Rome said the supplies, in the form of health kits, would be enough for 300,000 people for a month.

The Italian news agency ANSA reported that Italian armed forces were preparing to make military units available to the European Union as part of a multinational force to secure the passage of humanitrian-aid to the troubled Balkan country.
Eyewitnesses in Brindisi said a number of Italian naval vessels had recently docked at the port.
European Union foreign ministers are due to meet on Monday in Brussels to provide a blueprint for security measures to assist a major humanitarian relief mission in the wake of the unrest in Albania.
